trickyParts: Oh My Pi de-duplicates extensions by absolute path, not realpath, and loads installed plugins before explicit ones: with discovery on, a plugin both linked into the profile and named by --extension loads twice (two module instances, two factory runs). The image therefore stops linking pi-envoy and pi-legion; the probe prints one LEGION_ENVOY_PUBLISHER line per Envoy entry that published and the pod lane refuses more than one; a re-linked pi-legion alone is undetectable (its load marker is one overwritten object), so the two links come and go together in the Dockerfile.

The pairing lever is an OK-line mark (extensions=discovered), not a DaemonAPIVersion bump: the daemon's probe pod refuses an image whose CLI predates the discovery-on lane, since such an image's profile links the plugins a pod of this daemon would load twice.

flock does not cross pods under gVisor, so the warm-up's cross-process guard is an O_EXCL lease file with a 10 s mtime heartbeat and a 60 s stale takeover by rename (exactly one of two contenders wins the rename). dirExists is computed before the lease's directory is created, since nextCodegraphStep's fallback reads an existing .codegraph/ as an index to repair. Release removes the file only when os.SameFile says it is still the one created, so a holder stalled past 60 s and taken over cannot delete its successor's lease.

The shim starts the warm-up on the child's first frame (Oh My Pi's ready, once extensions are loaded), guarded by a sync.Once, under the shim's own loop context: when the child exits the loop ends, the warm-up's codegraph child is SIGTERMed (cmd.Cancel; killed after 5 s), the deferred release removes the lease, and Run waits for the goroutine (bounded at 10 s) before returning the agent's status. Round 1 claimed the deferred release ran on its own after a group SIGTERM; it did not — the shim exited the moment Oh My Pi did and the goroutine died with it (the tester's finding). Only a holder killed outright now leaves a lease, which the 60 s takeover handles. A SIGTERMed `codegraph init` can leave the database reported malformed; the next warm-up's `codegraph index` repaired it to complete.

get_state's data.systemPrompt is an array of strings on this Oh My Pi, not one string; the proof parser joins it. get_state.dumpTools lists only the built-ins, so the system prompt is the proof surface for extension and MCP tools, as the plan said.

This pod's installed pi-legion declares daemon API contract 14 while the branch's DaemonAPIVersion is 15 (from #1752), so the in-pod probe-image runs pass --daemon-api-version 14; the image built from this branch carries 15.

A rename is not an exclusive step on this filesystem: it moves whatever is at the path, a winner's fresh lease included, so two contenders that both judged one lease stale could both take it over and both build. The only exclusive step is O_EXCL create, so the takeover runs under a second such create, the marker; under it the lease is re-stat'd and removed only while it is the file judged stale. A marker older than warmLeaseStale is a contender killed inside those syscalls and is removed before the retry.

The pod's stop grace is `worker_stop_timeout_seconds` (10 s by default), not the launcher's 30 s unset fallback; the launcher now passes the shim `--stop-grace` so the drain is derived from it: 10 − 5 (agent grace) − 1 (stdout drain) = 4 s. Ending the warm-up when the agent is told to stop, rather than when it exits, keeps the worst case (an agent ignoring SIGTERM for its whole grace) at 5.6 s measured.

A lease must never be judged by its inode: v9fs (the tree volume) hands a file created at a path the inode the removed one had, so os.SameFile reads a successor's fresh lease as the file it replaced. The takeover re-judges by mtime under the marker; a holder knows its own lease by the token it wrote at the create (the release guard), so a stalled holder taken over cannot remove its successor's lease either. A test of a file-identity guard belongs on the filesystem the guard runs on, or pins the identity itself (the tester's hard link).
